problem: The flowchart moves straight from 'Integrability test' to 'Exact?' with no failure branch, so it suggests every Pfaffian passes the test and gets a surface. The Lead and Section 1 both say a nonzero result means no surface.

problem: 'A zero test gives local surfaces; a global surface may fail where P, Q, R are not smooth' is muddled: the test does not give surfaces, it only guarantees a local integrating factor.
fix: A zero test guarantees only local surfaces; a single global surface may fail to exist where P, Q, R are not smooth.

problem: 'It lets a non-exact equation be integrable' is confusing: a test cannot make an equation integrable.
fix: A form can pass this test and still be non-exact, so integrability is weaker than exactness.
